title: Sourdough Fermentation Environment Trend
dataSources: Sourdough monitor (`sourdough:reading`), BBQ/sous-vide probes (`bbq:probe`), fridge/freezer/oven temperature (`kitchen:appliance`), espresso shots (`espresso:shot`), pantry inventory (`pantry:item`), kombucha brew (`kombucha:reading`).
app: ESP32/ESPHome kitchen sensors (sourdough rise, BBQ/sous-vide probes, fridge/freezer temperature), espresso-shot logs, and pantry inventory via MQTT and Splunk HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=sourdough:reading
| timechart span=30m avg(temp_c) as temp, avg(humidity_pct) as humidity
| eval warm_enough=if(temp>=24,1,0)
description: Trends the temperature and humidity around your starter so you can explain why it rose fast one day and sluggishly the next.
value: Fermentation speed is driven by warmth; trending the jar's environment turns an inconsistent starter into a predictable one.
implementation: Ingest temperature and humidity from the sourdough sensor; review the environment trend alongside rise behaviour.
visualization: Dual-axis line chart of jar temperature and humidity over time.

references.title: Grafana Labs — monitor a sourdough starter

grandmaExplanation: It records how warm and humid it is around your starter, which explains why it grows quickly some days and slowly on others.
